packets.subject: Mathematics
packets.focus: Place value and total value through ten-thousands
packets.goal: Explain the place and actual value of each digit in a five-digit whole number.
packets.notes: A digit has a position and a value. In 43,562, the 4 is in the ten-thousands place and represents 40,000, while the 3 is in the thousands place and represents 3,000. A place-value chart helps us see the groups. Moving a digit one column to the left makes its value ten times as large. We read numbers carefully because the same digit can represent different amounts in different places.

model.prompt: A school collected 43,562 bottle tops for a reuse project. What is the total value of the digit 3?

steps.action: Write 43,562 in columns: ten-thousands 4, thousands 3, hundreds 5, tens 6, ones 2.
steps.why: Each column names the size of one group.

steps.action: Find the 3: it is in the thousands column.
steps.why: The position, not just the written digit, determines its value.
Three groups of one thousand make three thousand.

steps: Make the place-value headings from ten-thousands to ones.
Swap the 3 and the 5 and discuss how each digit's total value changes.
activity.evidence: Learner labels each column and explains at least one change aloud or in writing.

guided.prompt: In 25,641, which place holds the digit 5?
guided.reason: 5 is second from the left in this five-digit number.

independent.prompt: What value does the digit 7 have in 17,438?

independent.reason: There are zero tens, so that place adds nothing.

check.prompt: A learner says that the 8 in 48,020 is worth 8. Is that correct?
check.reason: The 8 sits in the thousands column.

packets.misconception: Confusing a digit with its total value. Point to the column and physically group thousands before multiplying.
packets.remedial: Build three four-digit numbers with digit cards, circle the thousands digit and say its value before moving to five-digit numbers.
packets.enrichment: Find two five-digit numbers containing a 6, where its value is different in each, and explain the difference.
packets.teacher: Ask what would happen if 3 moved one place left. Avoid teaching the place names as a chant without showing groups. Mark an answer correct only if the learner identifies both the place and value.
packets.accessibility: Use large clear columns, tactile counters or a spoken chart. Do not make access depend on a printed worksheet.

visual.description: Five-column chart labelled ten-thousands to ones, with 43,562 aligned; optional counters show 3 groups of 1,000.

packets.subject: English
packets.subStrand: The Family: Pronunciation and Vocabulary — Listening Comprehension
packets.focus: Attentive listening, helpful questions and accurate retelling
packets.goal: Listen to a short exchange about family routines, identify two details and respond clearly.
packets.notes: Good listeners allow a speaker to finish, notice important words and ask a clear question when something is missing. A helpful response can be short and respectful. Families organise chores in different ways, so describe what you heard instead of assuming who must do each task.

model.prompt: Read or listen: Amina: 'Could you help me arrange the cups, Otieno?' Otieno: 'Yes. I will arrange them after I wash my hands.' Amina: 'Thank you. I will bring the water.'

steps.why: You need the whole message before deciding what happened.

steps.action: Identify the two promises: arranging cups and bringing water.
steps.why: Remembering actions helps you retell accurately.

steps.action: Retell in one sentence: 'Otieno will arrange the cups and Amina will bring water.'
steps.why: A good summary keeps essential details without changing the speakers.

model.answer: Otieno will arrange the cups; Amina will bring water.
model.check: Re-read the exchange to confirm who does which task.

steps: Teacher reads the dialogue at a natural pace twice.
Learners tell a partner who will arrange cups and who will bring water.
Pairs exchange roles and practise a different polite request about a household task.
activity.evidence: Learner correctly recalls two details and asks or answers a respectful question.

guided.prompt: Who says 'I will bring the water'?
guided.reason: Her line begins with her name.

independent.prompt: Write one polite request that could be used at home.
independent.answer: Example: 'Could you please help me put away the books?'
independent.reason: A complete request explains what help is needed and uses a courteous tone.

independent.prompt: Why does Otieno wash his hands before touching cups?
independent.reason: The action supports hygiene in the family's routine.

check.prompt: Retell the dialogue in two accurate sentences without changing who promised what.
check.answer: Accept any two sentences that correctly assign the cups to Otieno and the water to Amina.
check.reason: Accuracy matters more than memorising exact wording.

packets.misconception: A learner repeats a line but swaps the speakers. Read the named turns again and use two name cards.
packets.remedial: Give two picture prompts and ask two who-did-what questions before attempting a full retell.
packets.enrichment: Invent a fourth line that politely checks whether the cups are ready; explain why it is respectful.
packets.teacher: Read rather than display the text on the first listen. Do not grade pronunciation on accent; assess intelligibility, content accuracy and respectful turn-taking.
packets.accessibility: Offer a second reading, visual name cards, or signed/pointed answers before requesting a spoken response.

visual.description: Two speech bubbles labelled Amina and Otieno, plus icons for washing hands, cups and water.

packets.subject: Kiswahili
packets.focus: Kutamka maneno kwa uwazi na kusikiliza kwa makini
packets.goal: Kutamka maneno ya kawaida kwa uwazi na kusikiliza mwenzake bila kumkatiza.
packets.notes: Matamshi bora humsaidia msikilizaji kuelewa ujumbe. Unapotamka neno, sikiliza sauti zake na zingatia silabi. Kwa mfano, 'kalamu' lina silabi ka-la-mu; 'kitabu' lina silabi ki-ta-bu; 'meza' lina silabi me-za. Lengo si kupima lahaja ya nyumbani bali kufanya mawasiliano yaeleweke kwa heshima.

model.prompt: Taja silabi za neno 'kalamu' na utumie neno hilo katika sentensi.

steps.why: Kusikia neno lote hutuwezesha kutambua sauti zake.
Kila kundi la sauti linasaidia kutamka neno kwa mpangilio.
Sentensi inaonesha maana ya neno katika mawasiliano.

materials: Kadi zenye maneno au uandishi ubaoni
steps: Mwalimu aseme 'kitabu', 'meza' na 'kalamu' kwa mwendo wa kawaida.
Wanafunzi wafanye mazoezi ya kusikiliza na kutenganisha silabi kwa makundi.
Kila mwanafunzi atunge sentensi moja na amsikilize mwenzake bila kumkatiza.
activity.evidence: Mwanafunzi anatenganisha silabi kwa usahihi na kutamka sentensi inayoeleweka.

independent.reason: Kubali sentensi nyingine yenye matumizi sahihi ya neno.

check.prompt: Tamka 'kalamu' kisha litumie katika sentensi fupi.
check.answer: Mwanafunzi atamke neno kwa uwazi na atunge sentensi yenye maana.
check.reason: Tathmini uwazi na maana ya mawasiliano, si lafudhi ya nyumbani.

packets.misconception: Kuchanganya kusoma silabi na kutamka neno. Mwalimu aonyeshe jinsi silabi zinavyounganishwa kutengeneza neno.
packets.remedial: Anza na neno lenye silabi mbili, 'meza', kabla ya maneno ya silabi tatu.
packets.enrichment: Tafuta maneno mawili ya vitu vya darasani yenye idadi tofauti ya silabi na uyalinganishe.
packets.teacher: Tumia maneno yanayofahamika; zingatia usikivu na matamshi yanayoeleweka. Usidharau lugha ya nyumbani ya mwanafunzi.
packets.accessibility: Ruhusu kushika kadi, kuonesha silabi au kusikiliza mara nyingi; tumia maandishi makubwa na ishara panapohitajika.

visual.description: Kadi za ka, la, mu zinazounganishwa na kutoa neno kalamu.

packets.subject: Indigenous Languages
packets.focus: Attentive listening to a local-language song about cultural foods
packets.goal: Listen to a fluent local-language speaker, identify two food words and respond respectfully using accurately checked forms.
packets.notes: Food names and noun forms vary among Kenya's indigenous languages. This teacher-facilitated lesson must use the selected language's authentic words, spoken by a proficient speaker. Do not translate an English noun-plural rule into the language or invent a song. A short locally provided, appropriately licensed song or spoken account is the learning text.

model.prompt: A fluent speaker says a local word for a food, then uses its singular and plural forms.

steps.action: Play or deliver the speaker-checked example twice.
steps.why: A second hearing helps learners notice sounds without guessing.

steps.action: Ask learners to identify one food and repeat the exact source expression.
steps.why: The intended form must come from a competent speaker, not an English translation.

steps.action: Invite a short response in the language using the modelled form.

model.answer: A successful response accurately reflects the chosen language's verified food terms.
model.check: The competent language speaker confirms forms and meaning before any learner-facing use.

materials: Fluent speaker or rights-cleared local recording
Food photographs or real safe ingredients
steps: Invite a fluent speaker to introduce two familiar foods using the local language.
Learners listen, point to matching pictures and ask a respectful question.
Learners repeat one singular/plural pair after a speaker has validated the forms.
activity.evidence: Learner recognises two foods and uses one speaker-verified noun form appropriately.

guided.prompt: Point to the food named by the fluent speaker.
guided.answer: The corresponding picture; verified against the speaker's actual recording.
guided.reason: Meaning is checked against the authentic local-language source.

independent.prompt: With a fluent adult, record or write one accurately verified local food name and explain its meaning.
independent.answer: Accept a local-speaker-validated example with accurate meaning; there is no generic English-derived answer key.
independent.reason: Forms differ among languages and must be locally validated.

check.prompt: Describe one detail heard in the authentic local-language food account.
check.answer: Accept a relevant, accurately understood detail confirmed against the actual account.
check.reason: A listening task assesses understanding, not invented vocabulary.

packets.misconception: Assuming all indigenous languages pluralise nouns as English does. Let the fluent speaker provide the actual forms.
packets.remedial: Allow repeated listening, familiar food pictures and a shorter two-word phrase.
packets.enrichment: Ask the speaker about a respectful food-sharing expression and identify when it is used.
packets.teacher: This packet is teacher guidance ONLY until the selected language is specified, vocabulary and orthography are checked, and text/recording rights are confirmed. Do not release unchanged to learners.
packets.accessibility: Use tactile food models or large pictures; use an accessible speaker-led alternative if audio playback is not available.

visual.description: Photographs or drawings of two local foods, labelled only after a fluent speaker verifies spelling.
